Subject: Re: SageMed dedicated tranche request — sizing notes

Sean / team,

Quick sizing notes after a brief look at SageMed's feature description (Tom's note):
- Baseline: 8x A100-equivalent to hit 5–10 qps sustained with <100ms p95 when using full-precision models and 4k context.
- Conservative reduction: we can shrink to 6 GPUs if SageMed accepts mixed-precision (Q4x8) + aggressive prefix caching and a 2k context cap — should keep p95 ~130ms.
- Shared-tenant alternative: multi-tenant isolates via strict KV cache namespaces and runtime QoS. This reduces cost but provides slightly less isolation guarantees (acceptable for many customers, likely not for regulated health setups).

Attachments: SageMed_Sizing.xlsx (estimated memory/throughput curves and cost delta matrix).

If Helio's tranche is contractually locked with an explicit tranche window, my default recommendation is to explore a staged launch for SageMed: 2-week pilot on shared tenancy (low ramp), followed by a dedicated 6-GPU tranche with scheduled increases to 8 GPUs by week 6. That gives Helio breathing room while satisfying SageMed's immediate production need with minimal risk.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Escalation: tranche precedence decision required

Team —

We need a clear, documented precedence call here. HelioAnalytics (RDW-2027-HE) has a reserved tranche in contract with a Q4 reservation clause and materially higher committed MRR. From a revenue and SLA standpoint, Helio has stronger precedence than a new Mid-Market deal (SageMed), unless SageMed's contract includes a signed SOW with tranche windows (I don't see one yet).

Action items:
1) Karthik — please confirm Helio reservation dates and any flexibility in maintenance/upgrade windows where we can temporarily reshuffle capacity.
2) Ben — refine the pilot + staged ramp plan and surface any risk that could cause SLA misses for SageMed.
3) Monica / Sean — if we offer SageMed a short-start tranche, consider commercial offsets (one-time onboarding credit, discounted first month) so Helio's commercial expectation isn't undermined.

We should aim to present a single recommended path to both parties by EOD tomorrow. This is an escalation to product/ops because resource succession will require scheduled reconfiguration in the fleet.

Laura
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 12:31:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Escalation: tranche precedence decision required

Laura / team —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick feasibility readout from capacity planning:
- Helio's tranche (scheduled 10/11 start) is within a cluster that currently sits at 72% utilization for the next two weeks and is forecast to hit 85% during scheduled model refresh windows mid-Oct. That means preempting or carving out 2 GPUs from Helio in the launch week would risk their p95 if done without compensating changes.

Proposed resource-succession plan (highest chance of keeping both customers happy):
A) Short pilot + burst lane for SageMed (start Oct 14): 2 dedicated GPUs + burst to 6 GPUs during low Helio activity windows.
B) Week 3 schedule for a staged expansion to 6 GPUs dedicated to SageMed as Helio's non-peak maintenance window is used; full 8 GPUs only after Helio's model refresh completes (week 6).
C) Operational mitigations: we enable stricter batching controls for Helio during the overlap and a safety fallback routing policy to the Hosted tier if latencies spike — logging will flag any SLA drift and auto-trigger rollbacks.

Commercial trade: to make this palatable, suggest offering SageMed a 20% onboarding credit for month 1 and a 10% permanent reduced unit-price for Q4 if they accept the staged ramp. For Helio, propose a priority assurance addendum with a minor credit if any tranche interference occurs (keeps their trust intact).

I've attached a draft "succession_plan_v1.docx" with the exact windows and runtime knobs. If Laura signs off, operations can schedule the cluster reconfig for Oct 13 maintenance window.

Karthik
Capacity Planning Manager — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
[attachment: succession_plan_v1.docx (docx)]

Subject: Re: SageMed dedicated tranche request — mediation proposal

Tom — thanks for the details and patience while we reviewed internal capacity. 

High level recommendation we can offer today: a staged onboarding that balances Helio's contractual reservation and SageMed's need for a production-safe start:
1) Pilot: Oct 14 — Oct 28: 2 dedicated GPUs for SageMed with burst-capacity to 6 GPUs during Helio non-peak windows.
2) Staged expansion: Oct 29 — Nov 11: increase to 6 dedicated GPUs (operationally scheduled).
3) Full dedicated tranche to 8 GPUs: targeted week of Nov 15, contingent on Helio's model refresh completion.

Commercially we propose a 20% onboarding credit for month one and reduced unit-pricing for Q4 contingent on accepting the staged plan. We will incubate the pilot under a higher-touch runbook (SE weekly check-ins) and a rollback policy if latencies exceed agreed thresholds.

If that sounds workable, I'll have contracts/procurement coordinate the MoU and get a DocuSign link out; operations is ready to book maintenance on Oct 13.

Sean
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
